simple.meaning: רְשַׁם (rᵉsham) is a Hebrew action word meaning “sign, write.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 7 times in Daniel, beginning at Daniel 5:24. The surrounding contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רְשַׁם (H7560) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: רְשַׁם (rᵉsham) / H7560 is traced through Daniel 5:24, Daniel 5:25, Daniel 6:9, Daniel 6:10 with source-language evidence and verse context.

occurrences.englishText: Then the part of the hand was sent from before him, and this writing was inscribed.
“This is the writing that was inscribed: ‘MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN.’
Therefore king Darius signed the writing and the decree.

When Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house (now his windows were open in his room toward Jerusalem) and he kneeled on his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did before.
Then these men assembled together, and found Daniel making petition and supplication before his God.

Then they answered and said before the king, “That Daniel, who is of the children of the captivity of Judah, doesn’t respect you, O king, nor the decree that you have signed, but makes his petition three times a day.”
Then the king, when he heard these words, was very displeased, and set his heart on Daniel to deliver him; and he labored until the going down of the sun to rescue him.
